subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-month-old boy is evaluated for prolonged bleeding after circumcision and a large intracranial hemorrhage. Factor IX activity is less than 1% of normal, and sequencing of the factor IX gene shows a single nucleotide change in the Kozak consensus sequence surrounding the AUG start codon that reduces binding of the small ribosomal subunit to the mRNA.
question: This mutation most likely decreases factor IX production by which mechanism?

options.text: Defective removal of introns from the transcript
Failure of polyadenylation at the 3-prime end
Misfolding of factor IX in the endoplasmic reticulum

explanation_correct: The Kozak sequence surrounds the AUG start codon in most eukaryotic mRNAs and facilitates binding of the small (40S) ribosomal subunit. A mutation that weakens this interaction impairs initiation of translation, so less factor IX protein is synthesized even though the mRNA is present in the cell.

explanation_incorrect.A: Transcription initiation depends on the promoter, such as the TATA box, and its transcription factors, not on the Kozak sequence at the start codon.
explanation_incorrect.B: Intron removal is performed by the spliceosome at splice sites; the Kozak sequence acts after the mRNA has been processed.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polyadenylation depends on the AAUAAA signal in the 3-prime untranslated region, whereas the Kozak sequence lies at the 5-prime end near AUG.
explanation_incorrect.D: Protein misfolding would affect stability or trafficking after translation; here the defect is at the initiation step of protein synthesis.

educationalObjective: The Kozak sequence facilitates 40S ribosomal subunit binding at the AUG start codon, so mutations that disrupt it impair translation initiation and reduce protein synthesis.
